correctness.rationale: For the constant spherical specialization, the source eigenvalue condition is a \(4\times4\) matrix equation. The source resolvent kernel separates into a scalar Yukawa part and an odd vector part. The double principal-value integral of the vector part vanishes by \(x-y\) antisymmetry, while the scalar double integral is exactly \(2\pi R^2(1-e^{-2\kappa R})/\kappa\). Diagonalizing \(\alpha_0\) leaves one admissible branch for each coupling sign. A half-angle substitution proves the branch function strictly monotone on the whole gap, yielding the exact threshold, uniqueness, multiplicity two, zero crossing, reflection symmetry, and both edge asymptotics. The numerical checker is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The sphere with constant coefficients is the canonical exactly symmetric geometry for the source's new non-local shell interaction. The result converts the abstract finite-dimensional determinant into a complete coupling phase diagram: a sharp existence threshold, exact twofold degeneracy, monotone traversal of the entire relativistic gap, an explicit zero crossing, and two edge scaling laws. These facts identify how a genuine bound state is born and moves under the model's most natural scalar coupling, rather than evaluating an arbitrary parameter point.
